newsitem.title: CHINA: China state offices say no role in HK-Taiwan links.
newsitem.headline: China state offices say no role in HK-Taiwan links.

text.p: Chinese government departments bolstered Hong Kong's promised autonomy on Friday by saying they had no role in the new special region's contacts with Taiwan, considered by Beijing a rebel province.
Hong Kong and Taiwan each named a high-level intermediary on Thursday to improve channels for cooperation after a surprise initiative by new Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung launched into talks with Taipei, just a day after predicting a quick deal on Taiwan's future status in China's newest and richest region on its return to Beijing control.
"Relations between Hongkong (Special Administrative Region) and Taiwan are a special component in ties between the two sides of the Taiwan Straits," said a Foreign Ministry official.
"The issue does not come under foreign affairs now."

The ministry said on Thursday central government approval was needed for official contacts between Taiwan and Hong Kong, which returned to Beijing rule on July 1 under a formula that gives it a high degree of autonomy.
Beijing has no official relations with Taipei and government departments that have had a role in Hong Kong and Taiwan affairs said they had no plans for managing ties between the two.
Many issues need to be ironed out in an economically crucial Hong Kong-Taiwan relationship that has became even more sensitive politically since the return of British-led Hong Kong.

Much of Taiwan's massive trade and investment with the mainland passes through Hong Kong. Taiwan trade is an important source of revenue for Hong Kong's container ports, banking and other service industries.
Foreign ministry officials referred requests for more information on how China would manage Hong Kong-Taiwan relations to the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet.

But the Taiwan Affairs Office said it had no role to play in how Hong Kong managed affairs with the island, Beijing's arch-rival since defeated Nationalist armies fled there during the Chinese 1949 communist revolution.
"We are not responsible for this issue," said a Taiwan Affairs Office official by telephone.

Issues dealt with by Hong Kong's new leadership, which has opened a dialogue with top Taiwan mainland affairs negotiator Koo Chen-fu, would be reported directly to the top leadership, said an official of the State Council's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office.
"We are not in charge of this kind of issue now," the official said.

The Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait (ARATS), which handles Beijing's unofficial contacts with Taipei, said it had not been informed about any new rules to govern Hong Kong-Taipei ties.
"We don't know about any new regulations on Taiwan and Hong Kong relations, except for what the Foreign Ministry spokesman said yesterday," an ARATS official said.

As a province of China, Taiwan is regarded by Beijing as a domestic issue and hence contacts with Hong Kong would not be seen as under the purview of foreign affairs. After the handover of Hong Kong this week, Beijing is responsible for Hong Kong's defence and foreign affairs.
